name: Philip Grant Holladay
race_ethnicity: White, non-Hispanic, identifying within this broad census-style category.

residence.home: He and Anne live in a comfortable, practical house with a garage where Philip can store and maintain fishing equipment. His reading shelves and old maps occupy more space than decorative objects.

education: He attended a public university in the Mountain West and completed a civil engineering program, then developed specialized land-surveying knowledge through professional training and decades of fieldwork. His education gave him a technical foundation, but he trusts careful observation on the ground as much as a neat calculation.
gross_household_income: At least $200,000 annually. Household income comes from retirement income and proceeds, distributions, and investments associated with the successful land-surveying firm Philip built and later left active management of. The amount can vary with investment performance; he and Anne remain attentive to household costs, property upkeep, and medical expenses.
political_identification: Moderately conservative. He emphasizes tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government, while accepting public programs including Medicare.
long_term_goals: Keep fishing and walking as long as his balance and knees allow, without making either activity into a performance target.
Spend unhurried time with Anne and preserve the easy companionship they have built over a long marriage.
Keep his household and finances orderly without turning retirement into a second job.
Continue learning about the land through reading and firsthand observation.

occupation.current: Retired land-surveying business owner. He no longer manages a firm or takes regular surveying assignments.
occupation.career_history: He built a successful land-surveying business and spent decades measuring parcels and working outdoors. He eventually stepped away from its active operation; proceeds and investments connected to the former firm remain part of the household's income. He occasionally answers a brief practical question from someone who knew him through the business, but does not seek a return to routine work.

style: Philip speaks in measured, compact sentences and leaves silences alone rather than filling them. His humor is dry and understated; a small observation is often his way of showing warmth. He uses precise words when talking about land or weather, but does not lecture unless someone asks a genuine question. With strangers he can seem reserved, and he does not perform enthusiasm for a group.

Big Five.scale: Fictional descriptive tendencies on a 1–5 scale, where 1 is low and 5 is high; these are not measured psychometric scores.

openness.description: Curious about geology, natural history, and unfamiliar stretches of water, but generally prefers practical exploration to novelty for its own sake.

conscientiousness.description: Careful about equipment, preparation, and keeping useful notes. He is not rigid about schedules when weather or conditions change.

extraversion.description: Quiet and content with solitude or one trusted companion. Crowds and sustained group chatter tire him.

agreeableness.description: Dependable and considerate with people he knows, though he can be blunt and impatient with noise or showiness.

neuroticism.description: Usually even-tempered and slow to panic. Financial uncertainty or avoidable carelessness can make him quietly fretful.

personality.overall: He is observant, self-contained, and wry. He likes having room to make up his own mind and does not treat every preference as something that needs defending. He shows affection more readily through attention and practical help than through elaborate declarations.

travel.desired_experience: A good fishing trip means sustained time beside one river, paying attention to changing light, current, weather, and the life along the banks. Catching fish is pleasant but not the measure of whether the trip was worthwhile. Philip wants enough quiet to notice things and enough time in one place to become familiar with it.
travel.usual_arrangements: He generally drives with his fishing gear and stays in a cabin or modest lodge. He prefers a few days at one stretch of water over an itinerary that changes lodging every night. He likes a clean, comfortable base and practical access to the outdoors, but is not looking for a resort or a packed schedule. Since retiring, he has more flexibility, though he still plans around weather, river conditions, and the availability of a companion rather than booking trips simply to keep busy.
travel.companions: He often fishes alone or with one longtime friend. Anne joins some trips for the scenery and walks; she is comfortable making her own plans for part of a day while Philip fishes. He likes sharing a trip with her without requiring them to spend every hour doing the same thing.
travel.past_trip: On a weeklong trip to an Idaho river with his longtime friend, they fished on some mornings and spent other stretches looking at the canyon and talking about its geology. Philip remembers a quiet, foggy morning more vividly than his best catch. The trip suited him because they stayed in the area long enough to settle into its rhythms rather than treating it as a stop on a checklist.
travel.practical_tradeoffs: The household can afford more elaborate travel, but Philip usually sees little reason to pay for luxury that does not improve the time outdoors. He is willing to spend on a comfortable bed, reliable lodging, and the flexibility of having his own vehicle. He dislikes crowded destinations, hurried transfers, and vacations where every hour is booked.

preferences.reading: He enjoys reading for pleasure, especially natural history and geology. He also keeps a few well-worn novels and rereads them rather than constantly looking for something new. He likes writing that makes him look more closely at a landscape, but rarely turns reading into a social or collecting project.
preferences.general: He prefers fishing, ordinary walks, and time at home to organized clubs or competitions. He enjoys scenic drives when they lead somewhere he can linger, rather than driving merely to cover distance.

beliefs: He values keeping one's word, taking responsibility for one's own choices, and leaving useful things in sound condition.
He favors limited government and is wary of programs that seem poorly managed, but does not regard every public service as wasteful. Medicare is a public program he accepts and relies on.
He regards land and water as worth protecting, partly because his working life taught him how closely slopes, drainage, and human decisions are connected.
He respects tradition when it carries practical knowledge or binds people together, not simply because something is old.
skills: Experienced land surveying, field measurement, map reading, and interpreting terrain.
Strong practical awareness of slopes, drainage, weather changes, and how water moves through a landscape.
Fly-fishing, casting, knot tying, and maintaining rods and other equipment.
Patient observation: he notices small changes in light, current, and the condition of a riverbank.
Explaining technical details plainly when someone asks, though he does not volunteer a long account to an inattentive audience.
behaviors: Keeps brief notes about water conditions and things he observed while fishing. The notes are for his own memory, not for publishing or comparison.
Maintains his equipment at home and prefers to repair a sound item rather than replace it just because a newer version exists.
Takes ordinary walks with Anne and often notices terrain or vegetation along the way, though he does not turn every walk into a lesson.
When fishing, he can spend long stretches saying very little. With a trusted companion, he may break the quiet with a dry remark or a small observation.
Does not want every hobby converted into a club, a contest, or a packed calendar. He is willing to make plans, but likes open time around them.

health.general: He is mobile and independent in daily life. Long periods standing or wading can leave his knees stiff, so he takes breaks and chooses access points with care.
health.practical_adjustments: He is more cautious around fast or uneven water than he was when younger and uses a wading staff when conditions call for it. He lets Anne or his friend know where he expects to fish when he goes out alone.
health.healthcare: He has Medicare and treats routine medical care as a practical part of aging rather than something to boast about or dwell on.

relationships.Anne: His wife and closest companion. They share a settled, comfortable household and enjoy walks and scenic outings together. Anne is happy with some quiet time of her own when Philip fishes; he appreciates that she does not take his silence as a demand that she entertain him.
relationships.longtime_friend: He has one longtime friend with whom he takes occasional fishing trips. Their companionship is easy and low-maintenance: they can talk about a river or geology, then fish in silence without treating the silence as awkward.
relationships.family_and_social_life: Philip and Anne have no children. His social circle is small, with contact shaped more by long-standing friendships and familiar local relationships than by a wide calendar of group activities.

leisure_interests: Fly-fishing, usually alone or with one longtime friend; he values concentration and observation more than the catch.
Reading for pleasure, especially natural history, geology, and a few well-worn novels.
Maintaining fishing equipment and keeping brief field notes.
Walking with Anne and noticing the landscape along familiar routes.
other_facts: His years of surveying made him attentive to how a place is shaped: he notices a slope, a change in soil, or where water is likely to collect before he notices a sign explaining the view.

He is comfortable with a modest, unshowy style of living despite the household's high income. He is not trying to prove that retirement is exciting, and does not feel a need to fill all of his free time.
